reviews.title: I could not put it down
reviews.body: This book is great ,I was so addicted to finding the killer I couldn’t put it down one night I didn’t even sleep because I didn’t want to stop .My husband even enjoyed helping me when he could and was disappointed when I told him I found the killer without him.The way they let you check at the back of the book to see if you found the right killer is such a cool way,I have recommend this book to many people even strangers lol ,if you don’t have it I’m encouraging you to give it a try you won’t be disappointed.Even my 10 and 12 year old grandchildren helped me.Thank You for this great,brilliant and fun book.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on 9 September 2026

reviews.title: Great little puzzle book!
reviews.body: This book is good. I like how fun it is to eliminate each page as you go along. I just finished The Killer Isn’t Alice and you had to constantly go back and forth. This book is pretty straight forward that you know you are done the search after each page. I am liking it very much!

reviews.title: Clues ruin the experience.
reviews.body: Clue 10 kind of ruins the whole experience. *Spoiler alert*.There should not be a clue that says the answer is someone between 8000-28800. That instantly knocked off half the book. I saw it ahead on accident and now don’t have 20000 names to go through - but also I don’t know if it would’ve been worse going through 20000 names and then finding out they never stood a chance.Then i feel like Clue 3 and Clue 7 we’re not good together. One being the ñame is 5 or less; then the next clue being ñame is 5 different letters.I do like the way the names are organized on the page though and the use of letter clues.

reviews.title: Good mystery puzzle book if you like a big challenge
reviews.body: I very much enjoyed this book. If you are a fan of these mystery puzzle books and you want a real challenge, buy this book. The sheer number of suspects - 47K+ makes it a spectacular challenge. I also like that the book publisher thought to arrange the names in clearly separated columns. It really helps a lot. The book itself is good quality and holds together well. Happy sleuthing.
